# Ground detail material

Asset: `earth-detail.png`

Generated with the built-in image-generation tool. This is an illustrative ground material, not a photograph or survey of the village. The existing ground and satellite images are preserved for the Source imagery layer. The model uses tiled surface materials at every zoom level, with mapped plot colours, vegetation distribution and illustrative furrows within the traced cultivated plot. A tile covers approximately two metres.

## Generation prompt

Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create one seamless tileable square PBR albedo ground texture for a realistic 3D model of a rural village in Andhra Pradesh, India. Orthographic camera pointing straight down at a 2 metre by 2 metre patch of dry hard-packed earth. Neutral muted warm grey-beige dusty soil, fine sand grains, many tiny irregular stone chips (2–12 mm), occasional small weathered pebbles, subtle compressed soil variation and a few thin dry straw fragments. Mostly compact smooth walking surface, restrained irregular hairline dry-soil fissures, no large rocks, no dramatic cracks. Photographic crisp microdetail with natural irregular distribution. Completely flat even diffuse lighting, no cast shadows, no perspective, no horizon, no vignette, no depth of field, no border, no text, no objects, no grass clumps, no tire tracks, no repeating conspicuous features. All four edges must tile seamlessly. Real photographic material scan, not illustration or stylized gravel. Full frame surface, high resolution.
